newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George wants tighter policy stance - minutes.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George wants tighter policy stance - minutes.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George continues to favour a marginally tighter UK policy stance now, according to the minutes of his September 4 monthly monetary meeting with Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke.

"The Bank continued to prefer a marginally tighter policy stance now and repeated the general point that the longer a tightening was delayed, the sharper it would eventually need to be," the minutes quoted him as saying. Official interest rates were left unchanged at 5.75 percent after the meeting.
George told Clarke that interest rates would have to rise "at some point" to give a better than even chance of meeting the 2.5 percent underlying inflation (RPIX) target.
"The Bank still expected RPIX inflation to fall to below 2.5 percent over the coming months," the minutes said.
But rising underlying domestic demand, beginning to feed through into output, put the inflation target "at significant risk in 1998."
"Taking all the evidence together, it would be very surprising if consumer demand did not continue to grow at well above trend," the minutes quoted George as saying.
"The real question was just how strong it would become."

Clarke said the boom in activity forecast by some people did not appear to be materialising. He said price data remained "extremely good" and noted that July output price inflation was the lowest since 1967.
"Recent surveys were more encouraging and any risk there had been of the economy slowing significantly had diminished," Clarke said.
Clarke agreed that consumer confidence was improving but noted that broad money growth had fallen back within its monitoring range.
He said increasing house prices were attracting attention but the evidence showed recovery was concentrated in particular sections of the market and particular areas.
"There was certainly no sign of any housing market boom," the minutes quoted Clarke as saying.
